items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between sessions; only what the program places in the new context is available. Options a, b and d each assume the model stores or learns from conversations, which is the misconception that assistants remember automatically.

Call 1 input is 1,000 + 100 = 1,100. Call 2 adds one tool step (450): 1,550. Call 3 adds a second: 2,000. Total 1,100 + 1,550 + 2,000 = 4,650. Answering 2,000 counts only the last call and forgets that every call resends the whole context; 1,100 + 450 + 450 = 2,000 shows the same slip.

Retrieval puts only the relevant pages in the context, which keeps cost down and avoids context rot. Pasting everything (b) pays for 600 pages in every call and dilutes attention; a notes file (c) is read back into the context so it has the same cost; training (d) does not contain this makerspace's manuals.

items.answer: It persists after the session ends, so a later session can read it back.
accepted: It keeps information after the conversation ends and can be read into a new context
It stores information outside the context window that lasts beyond the session
items.rationale: The context window is rebuilt for each call and gone when the session ends; a notes file lives outside it and lasts, so a later session can load it. Saying it is bigger than the window, or that the model learns from it, is wrong: the point is persistence.

A completed training date is a stable fact about one student that is costly to re-ask. Availability (a) goes stale and the calendar tool gives the live answer; the manual (b) belongs in retrieval; reasoning (c) is working detail of one session, not something the next visit needs.
